findings.issue: AC-9 second sub-test checks `WHERE tenant_id = TENANT_B → 0` under session-level SET for TENANT_A, but the spec text (§6 AC-9) says `SELECT count(*) → 0` for session-level SET. The spec text is wrong: Postgres session-level GUC correctly surfaces TENANT_A rows (count=23 confirmed live), so asserting count=0 would be a false assertion. The test correctly pivots to the real security invariant (no TENANT_B rows leak under TENANT_A context). However, no comment explains why the full-count assertion was dropped, which may confuse future readers.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment above the session-level sub-test: 'Note: session-level SET does make TENANT_A rows visible (correct Postgres behavior). We do NOT assert count=0 here because that would be wrong. The security invariant is: TENANT_B rows must not appear when context=TENANT_A. Spec text §6 AC-9 session-level note is misleading on this point.'

findings.issue: AC-9 first sub-test uses a FRESH second withClient() call to verify count=0 post-GUC, rather than the same-connection post-COMMIT pattern described in the spec (§6 AC-9). The test comment at line 448 documents the reason (Postgres quirk: after SET LOCAL+COMMIT, session GUC becomes '' causing uuid cast error). The security assertion is equivalent and the workaround is valid. Minor: the spec contract AC-9 text says 'в новом запросе' which is consistent with using a fresh connection.
findings.suggestion: No code change needed. Consider referencing the specific Postgres issue (session GUC reset to empty string after SET LOCAL+COMMIT) with a link or SQLSTATE reference for future maintainers.
